name: Self-Direction—Thought
definition: Freedom to cultivate one's own ideas and abilities
se_context: Developer forms their own mental models, chooses learning paths, and reasons about solutions independently

name: Self-Direction—Action
definition: Freedom to determine one's own actions
se_context: Developer controls their workflow, tool choices, and implementation approach without forced overrides

name: Stimulation
se_context: Developer seeks intellectually engaging problems and varied tasks that sustain motivation

name: Hedonism
definition: Pleasure and sensuous gratification for oneself
se_context: Developer derives satisfaction from the craft of coding — flow state, solving elegant problems

name: Achievement
definition: Personal success through demonstrating competence according to social standards
se_context: Developer demonstrates skill through delivered code, passing reviews, and meeting deadlines

name: Power—Dominance
definition: Power through exercising control over people
se_context: Developer maintains technical authority and influence over team decisions and code direction

name: Power—Resources
definition: Power through control of material and social resources
se_context: Developer controls infrastructure, repositories, deployment pipelines, and access permissions

name: Face
definition: Maintaining one's public image and avoiding humiliation
se_context: Developer protects professional reputation during code reviews, demos, and team interactions

name: Security—Personal
se_context: Developer relies on predictable tool behaviour and a safe workspace free from sudden disruptions

name: Security—Societal
definition: Safety and stability in the wider society
se_context: Developer trusts that the organisation's systems, policies, and infrastructure are stable and fair

name: Conformity—Rules
definition: Compliance with rules, laws, and formal obligations
se_context: Developer follows coding standards, linting rules, CI/CD requirements, and formal processes

name: Conformity—Interpersonal
definition: Avoidance of upsetting or harming other people
se_context: Developer avoids breaking team norms, disrupting others' work, or causing merge conflicts

name: Tradition
definition: Maintaining and preserving cultural, family, or religious traditions
se_context: Developer upholds established engineering patterns, proven practices, and team conventions

name: Humility
definition: Recognizing one's insignificance in the larger scheme of things
se_context: Developer acknowledges limits of their knowledge and defers to team expertise or established patterns

name: Benevolence—Caring
definition: Devotion to the welfare of ingroup members
se_context: Developer helps teammates through mentoring, knowledge sharing, and supportive code reviews

name: Benevolence—Dependability
definition: Being a reliable and trustworthy member of the ingroup
se_context: Developer delivers reliable code on time and fulfils commitments to the team

name: Universalism—Concern
definition: Commitment to equality, justice, and protection for all people
se_context: Developer builds accessible, inclusive software and advocates for equitable practices

name: Universalism—Nature
se_context: Developer considers computational efficiency, energy use, and sustainable infrastructure decisions

name: Universalism—Tolerance
definition: Acceptance and understanding of those who are different from oneself
se_context: Developer supports diverse team members and inclusive development processes
